items.stem: A manager asks Claude for a market-size figure and pastes the reply into a board deck unchanged. What is the main professional risk?

options.text: The figure may be fabricated or outdated and was never verified against a source
options.rationale: Correct: Claude can produce plausible but wrong figures, so any externally reported number must be verified before reuse.
Formatting is not the issue; accuracy and provenance are.

options.text: The deck will be too long
options.rationale: Length is unrelated to the verification risk described.

options.text: Claude will remember the figure for other users
options.rationale: Cross-user memory is not how the tool works and is not the risk here.

items.explanation: Correct: Claude can produce plausible but wrong figures, so any externally reported number must be verified before reuse.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of using an unverified Claude claim in a professional deliverable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Check reported figures and quotes against the original source
options.rationale: Correct: tracing claims to a source is the core verification step.

options.text: Ask Claude to confirm that it is sure
options.rationale: A model stating it is confident is not independent verification.
Correct: documenting AI assistance supports accountability and later review.

items.stem: A team needs a persistent workspace holding a client brief, reference files and an evolving memo that several people revisit over weeks. Which surface fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: Projects persist context and files for ongoing, shared work.
A one-off chat loses the shared, persistent context the team needs.
Email is outside Claude and does not provide the AI workspace described.
A routine is a practice, not a workspace surface.
